title: Introduce grace-prober and stall-resume-optimizer (regional hotfix)
author: Maya Chen
body: Context: During a recent regional spike (INC-8872) we observed a class of failures where overloaded nodes would prematurely drop connections while the control plane was still reconciling KV cache state. Symptoms included long tail latencies and an elevated rate of 'stalled-resume' errors when requests were re-admitted immediately after a circuit flip. Motivation: We need a low-risk, quick-to-rollout hotfix that reduces oscillation during regional pressure without changing tenant-facing admission semantics. This PR introduces two cooperating components: (1) grace-prober: a lightweight remote probe that exercises the fastpath on candidates before allowing full traffic rejoin; probes are inexpensive and additive to health probes, and (2) stall-resume-optimizer: a heuristic controller in the admission layer that enforces a short, tokenized resume-backoff for connections that previously saw KV drain or fastpath stalls. Design summary: - grace-prober runs as an in-process goroutine (non-blocking) that emits a single RPC to the local fastpath runtime; success is measured by a sub-5ms p90 response and a successful KV cache hit. Failure increments a regional 'probe-failure' metric and extends resume backoff. - stall-resume-optimizer maintains a small LRU of recently-evacuated connection IDs with a token bucket-like allowance per-tenant; when tokens are depleted, rejoin requests are delayed up to a configurable jitter window (default 250ms). - Both features are guarded behind runtime feature flags (runtime.enable_grace_prober, runtime.enable_stall_resume_opt) and a canary rollout is implemented via the node meta label (node.canary=true). Telemetry and alerting: - New metrics: runtime.grace_prober{result=success|failure}, runtime.stall_resume_delay_ms (histogram), runtime.stall_resume_token_usage. - Added a Grafana panel to the regional runtime dashboard and a low-severity alert that fires when probe-failure ratio > 5% for > 10m. Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to canary nodes in us-west-2 (node.meta.canary=true) for 4 hours, monitor probe success and p99 latency. 2) Gradual ramp to 25% nodes in the region over 2 hours if no regressions. 3) Global roll once telemetry is stable. Backout plan: disable runtime.enable_grace_prober and runtime.enable_stall_resume_opt via console flags, rollback node image if needed. Testing: - Unit tests for probe callback, token bookkeeping, and race conditions around LRU eviction. - Integration test that simulates KV drain and ensures the optimizer prevents immediate rejoin churn. - Load test in benchmark-lab that reproduces the INC-8872 pattern; we measured a 42% reduction in stall-resume error rate and a 18% drop in p99 tail under synthetic pressure. Checklist: - [x] Feature-flagged changes - [x] Basic unit + integration tests - [x] Perf/load test results attached - [x] Telemetry dashboards + alert added - [x] Canaries and rollout plan specified Changes: Small, focused runtime additions and admission controller wiring. See files_changed for specifics. Related: ENG-3921 (reduce rejoin oscillation), ENG-3898 (regional KV drain telemetry).

review_comments: Andre Patel (2026-01-18): Left a few nits but overall LGTM. Can you add a note about worst-case memory growth of the LRU?
Maya Chen (2026-01-18): Reply: LRU is capped at 1024 entries per-node by default; added a comment and test to assert cap behavior.
Priya Raghavan (2026-01-19): Please confirm telemetry cardinality - don't create per-tenant high-card metrics. Suggest aggregate by tenant_cohort instead.
Maya Chen (2026-01-19): Reply: Changed metric labels to tenant_cohort and added aggregation in the dashboard; updated tests.

merge_details: Merged by Maya Chen via squash on 2026-01-20. Commit message: 'hotfix: grace prober + stall-resume optimizer — reduce rejoin oscillation (ENG-3921)'.
release_notes: Hotfix: introduce a grace prober and stall-resume optimization to reduce oscillation during KV drain events. Default flags are off; enabled behind runtime flags and canary rollout. Reduces stall-resume error rate under pressure.
notes_for_ops: When enabling globally: monitor runtime.grace_prober{result=failure} and runtime.stall_resume_token_usage. If probe-failure >5% sustained, revert feature flag and investigate KV drift. Ensure canary nodes have node.meta.canary=true before enabling.
changelog_entry: 2026-01-20: hotfix(grace-prober): add probe and rejoin backoff heuristic to mitigate stall-resume errors (ENG-3921).
